requests.reason: Inspect snapshot interface contracts for what List availability and successful snapshot publication promise, keeping interface expectations distinct from file-store behavior.
Inspect the startup snapshot restoration consumer and surrounding initialization to establish fallback handling when a listed snapshot fails Open and locate any remaining recovery dependency.
Inspect file-store retention documentation, constructor constraints and configuration boundaries for an applicable retention guarantee and storage assumptions.

audit_question.question: When reclamation consumes file_snapshot_metadata_eligible, does the applicable retention or recovery contract require preserving an openable fallback if a higher-ranked eligible entry fails Open? The observed reaper permits displacement without state validation; the remaining discriminator is whether that scenario lies within a claimed recovery guarantee and permitted fault context.
audit_question.importance: An unusable retained prefix could cause deletion of an older readable snapshot and reduce startup recovery options. Actual recovery failure depends on the restoration consumer, remaining recovery evidence and applicable storage fault assumptions; none is established by the observed retention behavior alone.
contexts: A higher-ranked metadata-eligible entry whose state fails Open; legal reachability and fault applicability remain unresolved
event_paths: getSnapshots -> ReapSnapshots -> removal beyond retained prefix
FileSnapshotSink.Close -> finalize -> writeMeta -> Rename -> conditional parent Sync -> ReapSnapshots
FileSnapshotStore.Open -> state read -> CRC comparison -> rewind
counterevidence: getSnapshots excludes temporary directories and skips metadata decoding failures and unsupported versions.
The first Close reaches automatic reclamation only after finalize, writeMeta and Rename succeed, and after parent-directory Sync succeeds when enabled on non-Windows platforms.
finalize checks buffered Flush, enabled state Sync, file Close and Stat before recording size and CRC; errors prevent that Close invocation from reaching reclamation.

Open independently reads the state file, rejects CRC disagreement and requires a successful rewind before returning its reader. This protects that read boundary but is not invoked by retention selection.

Normal publication includes protections against exposing unfinished construction. The supplied source does not establish a permitted execution that defeats those protections and leaves every retained replacement unusable.
unknowns: Whether the snapshot interfaces or file-store documentation promise an openable retained fallback under state corruption, read failures or partial persistence.
Which permitted fault or interference history can produce a higher-ranked metadata-eligible entry that fails Open while an older entry remains readable.
Which caller serialization and storage assumptions apply to explicit ReapSnapshots calls and automatic reclamation.
Whether startup tries other listed snapshots after Open failure, and whether remaining logs or other recovery mechanisms can compensate.
The implementation of writeMeta is not attached; its successful return cannot yet be interpreted as a verified metadata durability guarantee.
The configured retention count, synchronization setting and platform for a concrete check remain unspecified.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: Cross-path review resolves the implementation discriminator: discovery reads metadata only, reclamation deletes beyond its ordered prefix without Open, and Open performs separate state validation. Given an unusable entry in that prefix, reclamation does not distinguish it from a usable one. Publication protections materially constrain how that state could arise, so contract and recovery-consumer evidence are needed before deriving an obligation.
